cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Corinth. He's got something to get off his chest, and he opens with a boast. His own conscience is taking the stand as his character witness.

cards.question: Paul says he's lived among the Corinthians in holiness and sincerity from God. He says he didn't run on worldly wisdom. So what did he run on?
Paul's talking about the letters he sends to Corinth. True or false: he says he writes them things beyond their ability to read and understand.

cards.text: Paul says they've understood him in part, and he hopes they'll understand him completely. Being half-understood is ROUGH, friend. It's like getting half a cookie recipe, and the half you got just says “preheat.”

cards.question: Paul looks ahead to the day of our Lord Jesus. What does he hope he and the Corinthians will do on that day?

cards.text: Confident of all that, Paul made a plan: stop in Corinth on the way to Macedonia, then swing back through Corinth on the way out. Two visits, one trip, and friend, the man had an ITINERARY.

cards.question: Paul planned to visit Corinth first so they might receive a ___ blessing.
After his second stop in Corinth, Paul wanted the church to help send him on his way. Where was he headed?

cards.text: Then Paul asks: did he make that plan carelessly, or plan by human standards, saying “Yes, yes” and also “No, no”? Baker, that's me and the snooze button: YES I'm up, NO I'm not, YES I'm up, no I'm NOT.

cards.question: Paul's asking whether his word flips back and forth. True or false: he says his message to the Corinthians is “Yes” and “No.”

cards.text: Then Paul points to the One he preached in Corinth with Silvanus and Timothy: Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Jesus was never “Yes” and “No.” In Him it has always been “Yes.”

cards.question: Paul says ___ the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ.

cards.text: So through Jesus, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God. And Paul says it's God who establishes both him and the Corinthians in Christ.

cards.question: Paul lists what God did for him and the Corinthians. What does he say God put in their hearts as a pledge of what is to come?
True or false: Paul also says God anointed them and placed His seal on them.

cards.text: Now Paul calls God as his witness about why he didn't come back to Corinth. When a man brings THAT witness, friend, you put the cookie down and listen.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he didn't return to Corinth?
Paul says he doesn't lord it over their faith. Instead, he and his team are fellow ___ with them for their joy.

cards.text: So Paul made up his mind about his next trip to Corinth. And unlike me at the topping station, once Paul's mind is made up, it STAYS made up.

cards.question: Paul decided not to make another ___ visit to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Then Paul asks a question. If he grieves the church, who's left to cheer him up?

cards.question: If Paul grieves the Corinthians, who does he say is left to cheer him?

cards.text: So instead of coming, Paul wrote them. He says he was confident in all of them, that they'd share his joy.

cards.question: True or false: Paul wrote so that when he arrived, he wouldn't be grieved by the people who ought to make him rejoice.

cards.text: And that letter wasn't easy, baker: Paul wrote it out of great distress and anguish of heart, through many tears. I teared up writing my goodbye on the back of a takeout menu in the drawer, and that was ONE paragraph.

cards.question: Paul wrote that letter through many tears. What does he say it was meant to show the Corinthians?

answers.text: How angry he was with them

cards.text: Now Paul turns to someone in the church who caused grief. Paul never names him, and neither will I.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the person who caused grief has mostly grieved Paul.

cards.text: The majority of the church already punished this man, and Paul says it's sufficient. That's the timer going off, friend: leave the batch in “just to be safe” and all you've got is charcoal.

cards.question: The punishment is enough. So what does Paul say the church ought to do now?
Paul says to forgive and comfort the man so he won't be overwhelmed by excessive ___.

cards.text: So Paul urges them to reaffirm their love for him. Back in the drawer, a scared can opener didn't need a lecture, friend; he needed somebody to say “Hey, you're with us,” not a list of every can he ever opened crooked.

cards.question: Paul says his purpose in writing was to see if they'd stand the test and be ___ in everything.

cards.text: And Paul's right there with them. Whoever they forgive, he forgives too.

cards.question: Paul says that whatever he's forgiven, he forgave for the church's sake, in the presence of someone. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul gives one more reason all this forgiving matters.

cards.question: Paul says they forgive so that someone won't outwit them. Who?
True or false: Paul says they are unaware of Satan's schemes.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 11 quotes "just to be safe", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states a fact from outside the passage, that Paul is "an apostle of Christ Jesus" (2 Cor 1:1). The card cites only 2 Corinthians 1:12 and gives no reference for that fact.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought ("For this is our boast"), but the opening card gives no context for why Paul is boasting or what he is answering. "He's got something to get off his chest" doesn't say what is going on.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Silvanus and Timothy appear here for the first time, but the card doesn't say who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says God put His Spirit in the hearts of Paul "and the Corinthians." The text says "our hearts" after "He anointed us" (1:21-22). Whether that "us" includes the Corinthians is left open by the text.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Paul also says God anointed them and placed His seal on them" uses "them," which points back to card 14. That card is no longer on screen. The card also treats the text's "us" as including the Corinthians, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Story card 1 gives no hint that the earlier visit was painful, so "another ___ visit" with painful/short/surprise can only be guessed from wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to the backstory: that Papa Dorin teared up while writing his goodbye note in the drawer. The drawer is not his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The text says "if anyone has caused grief" (2:5). The card drops the "if" and states as fact that someone in the church caused grief.
The setup joke (leaving the batch in "just to be safe" turns it to charcoal) and the card 12 question ("The punishment is enough") both rule out the wrong answer "Punish him once more."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke changes the can opener scene from the backstory. It invents a can opener with a record of cans "opened crooked" and gives Papa Dorin words ("Hey, you're with us") he didn't say in the backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Paul's purpose in writing. Choosing obedient over generous or patient depends on wording the baker hasn't seen, not on meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The text says "if I have forgiven anything" (2:10). The question says "whatever he's forgiven," which drops the "if."

The question says "they forgive so that someone won't outwit them." In 2:10-11, the purpose "in order that Satan should not outwit us" belongs to Paul's own forgiving, done for their sake in the presence of Christ. The card gives the reason to the church's forgiving instead.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
